newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-HINGIS BACK IN THE SADDLE BUT FINDS THE GOING HARD.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS BACK IN THE SADDLE BUT FINDS THE GOING HARD.

text.p: Martina Hingis discovered on Tuesday that being world number one and top seed does not guarantee an easy ride through the first rounds of Wimbledon.
Hingis, playing her first match since losing the French Open final, was lucky to scrape a 6-4 6-4 win over qualifier Anne Kremer, an amateur ranked 217 places below her in the world.

Australian Open champion Hingis, who went home to Switzerland after Paris to continue recuperating from a knee injury, needed six matchpoints to finish off Kremer, the sole representative of Luxembourg at the championships.
"It wasn't too easy for a first match," admitted Hingis.
It was arguably only Kremer's inexperience that allowed Hingis to advance. The 21-year-old Kremer hit almost as many double faults as good serves, including four in a row during the first set.
Kremer went 3-1 up in the opening set after Hingis had netted a backhand to concede a break in the third game.
The Luxembourg woman, who has won only three matches all year, held the upper hand several times throughout the one hour 33 minutes of play but was never able to capitalise on her advantage.
Hingis, who reached the fourth round here last year, served for the match at 5-3 but Kremer saved two matchpoints and then broke serve when the Swiss woman mis-hit a forehand.
Kremer saved three more matchpoints on her own serve in the following game, leaving Hingis screaming in frustration. But on the sixth the pressure got to Kremer and she put a forehand wide.
Hingis, seeded to meet Monica Seles in the final, said the knee which she injured in a riding accident in April had felt fine on her first outing on Wimbledon's new Court One.
And she said she had been horse riding again while at home. "If I'm still here on Sunday I'll go riding in Wimbledon," she added.
But first Hingis will play Olga Barabanschikova of Belarus. She is ranked only 80th in the world but, as Hingis nearly found to her cost on Tuesday, numbers mean little on the Wimbledon grass.
